title: Awarapan 2 Crosses Rs 100 Crore in India, Nears Rs 150 Crore Worldwide in 5 Days
excerpt: Emraan Hashmi scores his first solo hit as the sequel to the 2007 cult classic dominates the Independence Day box office window.
body:
• Awarapan 2 has collected over Rs 100 crore net in India and approximately Rs 144 crore in worldwide gross within five days of release
  • The film gave Emraan Hashmi his biggest solo opening ever, with an Rs 81.75 crore opening weekend
  • The sequel to the 2007 cult classic outperformed Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947 in the Independence Day box office clash

Emraan Hashmi's Awarapan 2 has crossed the Rs 100 crore net mark at the Indian box office in just five days, cementing the sequel as the actor's first blockbuster solo hit. The film's worldwide gross stands at approximately Rs 144 crore, according to tracking data from Sacnilk and Bollywood Hungama, putting it within striking distance of the Rs 150 crore milestone.

Released on August 14, 2026 — ahead of India's Independence Day — the Vishesh Films production has dominated the holiday box office window, comfortably outpacing all other new releases.

Day-by-Day Breakdown

The film opened to Rs 21.89 crore net on Day 1, a strong start for a solo Emraan Hashmi vehicle. Independence Day on August 15 delivered a massive 54% spike, with Day 2 collections surging to Rs 33.77 crore net — the film's single biggest day so far. Day 3 held steady at Rs 25.55 crore net, bringing the opening weekend to approximately Rs 81.75 crore net domestically.

Weekday collections on Monday and Tuesday naturally dipped from the holiday highs, but cumulative India net collections have now crossed Rs 100 crore. The film added approximately Rs 19 crore from overseas markets during the opening weekend alone, with particularly strong showings in the UAE, UK, and North America.

From Box Office Disaster to Franchise

The original Awarapan, released in June 2007 and directed by Mohit Suri, earned less than Rs 8 crore domestically and was labelled a commercial failure. Over the following 19 years, however, the film built a devoted cult following driven by its emotional intensity, memorable music by Pritam, and Hashmi's performance as the brooding gangster Shivam Pandit.

"The cult following of Shivam Pandit seems to be driving a massive wave of momentum for Hashmi."

— Sacnilk, trade analysis

Directed by Nitin Kakkar and co-starring Disha Patani, the sequel has transformed that long-tail cultural affection into genuine commercial returns. The nostalgia factor, combined with strong promotional assets and positive audience reception, propelled advance bookings past the 1 lakh ticket mark in national chains before opening day.

Winning the Independence Day Clash

Awarapan 2 emerged as the clear winner of the crowded Independence Day weekend, which also saw releases of Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947 and Suriya's Vishwanath & Sons in the South. Batwara 1947, backed by Aamir Khan and also starring Preity Zinta, managed approximately Rs 26.50 crore net in its opening weekend — well behind Awarapan 2's Rs 81.75 crore.

The film now ranks as the third highest-grossing Bollywood release of 2026 and holds the 32nd spot for highest opening weekends in Hindi cinema history.

Road to Rs 200 Crore

With no major Bollywood competition until Toxic arrives on August 26, Awarapan 2 has a clear theatrical window to continue its run. Trade analysts suggest the film has a realistic shot at challenging the Rs 200 crore net milestone domestically — a figure that would have seemed unthinkable for an Emraan Hashmi solo film just weeks ago.

For Hashmi, who defined an era of Bollywood with franchises like Raaz, Murder, and Jannat, Awarapan 2 represents a career-best commercial result. For many Gen Z viewers, this is the first time they are seeing him headline a major theatrical release — a passing-of-the-torch moment that has the trade paying close attention.
